title: agent-onboarding.md's blanket exit-6 remedy is wrong for the schema-drift class (lore sync regenerates no schemas)
description:
Filed from the LCLI-545 confirmatory review (opum-control review.recorded seq 7944, run job-133g1fq), which found it while checking whether the schema-drift remedy is named consistently across the surfaces that state it. NOT fixed there: it pre-dates that diff and sits outside it.

THE DEFECT. docs/runbooks/agent-onboarding.md:467 reads: "If it exits `6`, run `lore sync`, commit the result, and re-run." That is a BLANKET remedy for exit 6, but exit 6 covers several classes. `lore sync` regenerates no `.lore/schemas/` files -- `git grep -i schema src/commands/sync.ts src/core/sync.ts` returns nothing -- so for the schema-drift class it cannot clear the failure. The remedy for that class is `lore schema export` and committing `.lore/schemas/`, which the drift findings, the agent instructions, the `lore schema --help` summary and the spec decision table now all name in full (LCLI-545, PR opum-ai/lore-cli#530).

WHY IT MATTERS. A reader who follows the runbook on a schema-drift red runs `lore sync`, commits, re-runs -- and is STILL red, having changed nothing. That is the same "remedy at the point of need that does not clear the failure" family LCLI-545 exists to close, one document over.

SUGGESTED FIX: scope the runbook's exit-6 remedy to the classes `lore sync` actually fixes, and, for the schema-drift class, name `lore schema export` plus committing `.lore/schemas/` -- so the blanketed sentence stops promising a remedy that cannot work for one of the classes it covers.

NOT STAMPED: no assignee; opum-doc decides whether it is dispatched.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The exit-6 remedy in docs/runbooks/agent-onboarding.md no longer promises lore sync for every exit-6 class; it is scoped to the classes lore sync actually fixes.
For the schema-drift class it names lore schema export plus committing .lore/schemas/, matching the drift findings and the lore schema help summary (LCLI-545).
